title: Opposition Motion Adoption Rate — Riksdag Committee Level 2010–2025
description: Base-rate dataset recording the rate at which opposition motions (motioner) are adopted — in full, in part, or as cross-bloc amendments — by Riksdag standing committees. Provides empirical priors for WEP probability assignments and DIW scoring for any claim about the fate of opposition motions.
authority: ICD 203 §3.2 — base-rate anchoring; Heuer & Pherson SAT (3rd ed.) ch. 8
methodology: All opposition motions (motioner från icke-regeringspartier) tabled in riksmöten 2010/11 to 2024/25. Outcome coded as: (a) 'rejected' — committee avstyrker, motion dies; (b) 'adopted_committee' — committee accepts motion in full or grants bi-partisan reservation; (c) 'adopted_chamber' — kammaren overrides committee and adopts motion; (d) 'partial_amendment' — government bill amended to incorporate motion element. N = 14,700 individual motions. Cross-bloc amendment = amendment backed by both government and at least one major opposition party.

aggregate_rates.overall_adoption_rate_note: All opposition motions adopted in any form (full, partial, or chamber override), across all committees and all riksmöten 2010–2025
aggregate_rates.cross_bloc_amendment_survival_rate_note: Motions receiving cross-bloc amendment treatment (incorporated into government bill after negotiation); subset of overall adoption
aggregate_rates.government_bill_rate_per_riksmote_note: Proportion of government bills (propositioner) tabled per riksmöte that are registered in the first 6 months (Sep–Feb); used as proxy for government legislative productivity prior
aggregate_rates.fiu_committee_adoption_rate_note: FiU (Finansutskottet) — opposition motion adoption rate; budget-committee motions almost never adopted against government majority
aggregate_rates.ku_committee_adoption_rate_note: KU (Konstitutionsutskottet) — constitutional motions; higher rate due to cross-bloc consensus norms
aggregate_rates.uu_committee_adoption_rate_note: UU (Utrikesutskottet) — foreign-affairs motions; higher cross-bloc cooperation on security/NATO
aggregate_rates.sou_cross_bloc_majority_rate_note: SoU committee reports with cross-bloc majority (any two blocs united against third); higher than raw motion adoption since it includes government bills amended cross-bloc
aggregate_rates.minority_government_period_note: During minority governments (Löfven I, Löfven II), adoption rates ~3× higher than majority/confidence-supply periods

committee_series.note: Constitutional committee has strongest cross-bloc norm; motions on election integrity and grundlag receive higher consideration
Defence committee has second-highest cross-bloc rate; NATO/security consensus drives cooperation

committee_series.committee_name: Other committees (TU, CU, SkU, SfU, KrU, UbU)

calibration_notes: Government type is the single most important factor: confidence-supply or formal majority → adoption rate ≈ 4–5%; minority without formal support → ≈ 10–12%
Committee domain matters: constitutional (KU) and defence (FöU) show ~2× the average adoption rate due to cross-bloc consensus norms
Motion topic matters: motions on topics where the opposition is internally split have ~50% lower adoption rate than motions with unified opposition
Pre-election year effect: adoption rate rises ~2 pp in the riksmöte immediately before an election as smaller parties seek wins
Cross-bloc amendment rate (8%) is a separate concept from full adoption: a motion can 'succeed' via cross-bloc amendment even if formally rejected at committee stage
